assumptions: Deployment dep-1842 is related to the checkout service or a dependency of it (not explicitly stated in the evidence)
'Approximately the same time' for the database latency increase means it coincided with the 10:04 UTC checkout failure spike, not some other reference point
All four reported signals (deployment, checkout failures, DB latency, payment provider errors) belong to the same causal chain rather than being coincidental, independent events
The reported checkout failure rate (0.4% -> 9%) reflects a genuine service degradation and not a monitoring/measurement artifact
facts: At 10:04 UTC, checkout failure rate increased from 0.4% to 9%
Deployment dep-1842 completed at 10:01 UTC, approximately 3 minutes before the failure spike
Database latency increased at approximately the same time as the checkout failure spike
The external payment provider reported intermittent errors
The incident report explicitly states the root cause is not confirmed

hypotheses.claim: Deployment dep-1842 introduced a change (code, config, schema, infra) that caused the checkout failures
supporting_evidence: Deployment completed at 10:01 UTC, only ~3 minutes before the 10:04 UTC failure spike, showing temporal proximity
Deployments are a common trigger for sudden service regressions
contradicting_evidence: No evidence of what dep-1842 actually changed or whether it touched checkout-related code paths
Root cause explicitly stated as not confirmed
A 3-minute gap could reflect coincidence, cache warm-up delay, or an unrelated concurrent event rather than causation
Two other candidate causes (DB latency, payment provider) are present and unexplained by the deployment hypothesis alone

hypotheses.claim: Increased database latency directly caused (or contributed to) the checkout failures
supporting_evidence: DB latency increase is reported as occurring at approximately the same time as the checkout failure spike, indicating correlation
contradicting_evidence: No data on which database, magnitude of latency increase, or affected queries/tables
Direction of causality is unclear: DB latency could be a symptom of the same underlying cause (e.g., dep-1842) rather than the cause of checkout failures itself
No error logs cited confirming checkout failures were DB-timeout related

hypotheses.claim: Intermittent errors from the external payment provider caused (or contributed to) the checkout failures
supporting_evidence: Payment provider explicitly reported intermittent errors, and checkout inherently depends on payment processing, making this a directly plausible cause
contradicting_evidence: No timestamp given for when payment provider errors began, so temporal alignment with the 10:04 UTC spike is unverified
Could be an independent, coincidental external issue unrelated to the internal deployment/DB timeline

hypotheses.claim: The incident resulted from a combination of factors (deployment change interacting with DB latency and/or payment provider instability) rather than a single isolated cause
supporting_evidence: All three candidate signals (deployment, DB latency, payment errors) cluster within the same short time window around 10:01–10:04 UTC
contradicting_evidence: No evidence establishes an actual causal linkage or interaction between the three signals
Equally consistent with three unrelated, coincidentally-timed events
Insufficient granularity in timestamps to confirm sequencing or interdependency

Historical baseline/normal variance for DB latency and payment provider error rates for comparison

reversible_next_actions: Pull and review checkout failure error logs/status codes for the 10:01-10:10 UTC window to classify failures as DB-related, payment-related, or application-related

uncertainty.reason: The evidence provides only coarse temporal correlation between a deployment, a checkout failure spike, a database latency increase, and payment provider errors. No diagnostic data (logs, error codes, change details, precise timestamps) is available to establish causation versus coincidence, and the incident report itself explicitly states the root cause is unconfirmed. Multiple plausible, mutually non-exclusive hypotheses remain open.
